newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian government vows help to nuclear sector.
newsitem.headline: Russian government vows help to nuclear sector.

text.p: Workers from the Smolensk nuclear power station in western Russia claimed success for a cross-country protest march on Thursday when Moscow officials promised immediate aid to help ease huge wage arrears in the industry.

First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov told delegates of the angry workers, who marched 350 km (220 miles) from Smolensk to the capital, that 25 billion roubles ($4.3 million) will be allocated to Smolensk station at once, his press office said.
President Boris Yeltsin, also clearly worried by the state of affairs in the nuclear sector, told Nuclear Energy Minister Viktor Mikhailov to ensure things improved immediately.
Yeltsin, holidaying in the northwest, told Mikhailov to "pay specific attention to proper financing of the ministry's enterprises as well as ensuring state orders for them".
Nemtsov, who is also energy minister, promised to start allocating 123.5 billion roubles ($21.5 million) monthly to pay off debts to other nuclear power stations from this month.
He added that the figure would rise to 300 billion ($52.2 million) with effect from the last quarter of the year.
The news won applause from about 80 workers dressed in white lab coats who picketed the White House government building.
"The action was a complete success," Interfax news agency quoted trade unionist Igor Fomichev as saying.
"I believe the government will fulfill its promises and there will be no more need for such marches."
Another union official, Vyacheslav Vorobyov, told Interfax that the protesters will withdraw from central Moscow to their camp outside the city once a bank order for the cash arrived.
Vorobyov said they would return to Smolensk on Friday.

Apart from demanding back wages, some dating back six months or more, the protesters also demanded goverment action against consumers who do not pay their electricity bills, running up huge debts to the nuclear industry.
While the government's debt to nuclear workers, both in power stations and research centres, amounted to 250 billion roubles ($43.5 million), consumers owed them hundreds of millions of dollars.
Russia's two biggest nuclear research centres alone -- Arzamas-16 and Chelyabinsk-70 -- were owed 73 billion roubles.
Protestors have said poor financing could compromise safety at nuclear reactors -- although the march itself did not do so since only off-duty workers took part.

Arzamas-16 researcher Alexander Zakharov was conducting a weapons test last month involving a controlled nuclear chain reaction when he received a fatal dose of neutron rays. His was the first Russian death in a nuclear accident since the Chernobyl power station disaster in 1986.
